definition_one_sentence: A customer account with at least one non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.
formula_or_rule: count(distinct customer_id) from fct_orders where status <> 'cancelled' and order_date > today - 12 months and order_date <= today
example: On 2026-11-25: 1 080 of 1 233 accounts are active. A customer whose only order was cancelled is not active.
owner_who_decides: Sara Martin (Head of Sales) - aligned with Paul Girard (Head of Finance)
notes_conflicts: Sales memo: 6 months, any order. Finance memo: 12 months, non-cancelled. Decision: Finance rule, because the board and investors compare years. Sales keeps its 6-month view as a separate term 'recently active customer' = same rule over 6 months (775 accounts on 2026-11-25).

definition_one_sentence: Money ShopFast keeps from an order: what the customer paid, minus refunds, without VAT.
formula_or_rule: round((gross_revenue_eur - refunded_eur) / 1.20, 2); shipping included; cancelled orders excluded when summed over a period
example: EUR 120.00 paid, no refund -> 100.00. EUR 120.00 paid, EUR 60.00 refunded -> 50.00. Last 12 months: EUR 466 109.86 net vs EUR 589 805.56 gross.
notes_conflicts: Sales memo wanted VAT included (sales team paid on amounts incl. VAT). Decision: net revenue is always excl. VAT; Sales uses the existing term 'gross revenue' (VAT incl.) for commissions. Both memos agree: minus refunds, shipping included.

definition_one_sentence: A customer who has bought before but has no non-cancelled order in the last 12 months.
formula_or_rule: has at least 1 non-cancelled order with order_date <= today AND is not an active customer
example: On 2026-11-25: 1 225 accounts ever bought, 1 080 are active -> 145 churned. An account that never ordered is not churned.
notes_conflicts: Defined as the complement of 'active customer' among buyers so that active + churned = buyers. The churn ML model predicts this label.

definition_one_sentence: A person who has created an account on ShopFast, identified by one customer_id.
formula_or_rule: one row of dim_customers = one account (exact duplicate rows removed)
notes_conflicts: One person can still have 2 accounts (52 rows share an email under 2 ids - CTP 2 scorecard); merging them is a Steward decision, not automatic.

definition_one_sentence: One purchase placed by a customer on one channel, identified by one order_id, whatever its status.
formula_or_rule: one row of fct_orders = one order (duplicate order_id removed, first copy kept); cancelled orders excluded from revenue and from active customers
example: 5 200 orders, of which 434 cancelled -> 4 766 orders count for revenue.
notes_conflicts: 'canceled' (US) and 'cancelled' are the same status. 14 orders point to an unknown customer_id (relationships test set to warn).
